title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README to understand what hoopR is: a SportsDataverse R package that delivers tidy men's basketball data across NBA (2002-2026) and college (2006-2026) from ESPN, the NBA Stats API, the College Basketball Data API, and auxiliary sources. The landing page frames the two core access patterns the rest of the tour expands on — scraping live endpoints function-by-function, and bulk-loading pre-processed season releases. Read it first to get the map before diving into the code.

title: Shared ESPN Basketball Helpers
description: Before the per-league scrapers, hoopR factors the ESPN logic shared by NBA and MBB into one internal backend. espn_basketball.R is the documentation hub tying the families together, while the event, team, and athlete helper modules fetch and tidy ESPN Core v2 / Site v2 resources into tibbles that both leagues reuse. Understanding this 'one core + thin per-league wrappers' pattern is key — it explains why the next two steps look like mirror images of each other.
languageLesson: R packages keep internal helpers un-exported (no @export tag) so they stay private to the package namespace. Functions prefixed with a dot (.bb_*) are an additional convention signaling 'internal, do not call directly'.

title: ESPN Men's College Basketball
description: espn_mbb_data.R is the heart of the MBB ESPN surface: play-by-play, team/player box scores, rosters, scoreboard, schedule, rankings, standings, and the parsers that flatten ESPN summary payloads. It leans on the shared helpers from Step 2 and is complemented by focused wrappers like deep team resources, season metadata, and the per-game win-probability extractor. This is the highest-traffic college data path in the package.

title: ESPN NBA
description: The NBA ESPN surface mirrors the MBB one structurally — espn_nba_data.R provides play-by-play, box scores, rosters, schedules, and standings from ESPN Site v2, while the athlete and team-detail wrappers are direct counterparts to their MBB siblings. Building on the shared helpers from Step 2, this symmetry is deliberate: the same backend serves both leagues, so once you know the MBB shape you already know the NBA shape.

title: NBA Stats API
description: Beyond ESPN, hoopR wraps the official stats.nba.com endpoints for richer data. nba_stats.R is the index hub; utils_nba_stats.R is the shared HTTP and result-parsing layer that builds requests (with proxy support) and maps NBA Stats resultSets into tibbles. The player module is the largest wrapper, and nba_stats_pbp.R adds enriched and live cdn.nba.com play-by-play feeds. Note the recurring pattern: a utils layer owns transport and parsing, and thin endpoint modules sit on top.

title: College Basketball Data API
description: The cbbd_* family wraps the third-party College Basketball Data API. cbbd_api_key.R is foundational — it manages the API key and exposes the shared authenticated .cbbd_get helper that every other cbbd_* wrapper depends on (the highest fan-in node in the whole graph). The games, lines, and stats wrappers sit on top, returning schedule/box-score, betting-odds, and aggregate-stat frames respectively.
languageLesson: hoopR stores API keys in an environment variable read at request time (cbbd_key/has_cbbd_key), keeping secrets out of source and letting CI inject them via repository secrets rather than committing credentials.

title: Auxiliary Sources & Web Scrapers
description: hoopR also scrapes sources without clean APIs. Each family has a shared internal utils layer: bref_utils.R parses Basketball-Reference HTML tables, realgm_utils.R drives chromote page rendering for RealGM, torvik_utils.R centralizes barttorvik.com requests, and the kp_* family logs into KenPom with an httr2 cookie jar. This step shows how the same 'shared utils + thin scrapers' pattern from Steps 5-6 scales to heterogeneous HTML and authenticated sources.
languageLesson: R web scraping leans on rvest (CSS/XPath HTML parsing) and httr2 (modern request pipelines with cookie-jar sessions). chromote drives a headless Chrome for JavaScript-rendered pages that rvest alone cannot read.

title: Pre-Processed Data Loaders
description: Scraping live endpoints is slow; for whole-season analysis hoopR ships loaders that pull pre-scraped parquet/RDS assets from SportsDataverse-data releases. load_hoopR.R is the overview hub, while load_mbb.R and load_nba.R provide season-level play-by-play, box scores, schedules, rosters, and standings with parallel download and DBI database-build helpers. These are the functions the cookbook vignettes (Step 12) actually use — the fast path most users start with.

title: Utilities & Cross-Source Crosswalks
description: utils.R is the package-wide backbone — KenPom credential handling, cached URL loaders, season/year helpers, team-name normalization, and the hoopR_data S3 class with its print method. data.R documents the bundled team-links reference dataset. crosswalk_basketball.R is the deterministic normalization engine that the NBA and MBB crosswalk builders use to reconcile ESPN, NBA Stats, Fox, KenPom, and Barttorvik identities into one ID map — the glue that lets data from Steps 3-8 be joined together.
languageLesson: S3 is R's lightweight object system: a class is just an attribute on a value, and dispatch happens by naming a method generic.class (here print.hoopR_data). It needs no formal class declaration — the print method is registered in NAMESPACE.

title: Package Manifest & Namespace
description: Two generated/authored config files define hoopR as an installable R package. DESCRIPTION is the manifest: version 3.1.0, MIT license, R >= 4.1, and the Imports/Suggests (httr2, dplyr, rvest, data.table) that power every layer you have seen. NAMESPACE is roxygen2-generated and exports the 270+ functions across the bref_/cbbd_/espn_/kp_/nba_/load_/torvik_/realgm_ families plus the print.hoopR_data S3 method, controlling exactly what users can call.
languageLesson: In R packages DESCRIPTION declares dependencies and metadata, while NAMESPACE — regenerated from roxygen2 @export/@importFrom tags, never hand-edited — governs which functions are public and which packages' symbols are imported.

title: Worked Examples: Vignettes
description: Vignettes are hoopR's runnable tutorials and the best end-to-end view of how the layers combine. getting-started walks installation and a quick-start; the MBB and NBA cookbooks stitch loaders (Step 8), ESPN data (Steps 3-4), NBA Stats (Step 5), and KenPom metrics (Step 7) into real analysis workflows. The ESPN-endpoints, CBBD, and KenPom vignettes document those specific surfaces by use case. Read these to see the package used the way an analyst would.

title: CI/CD & Docs Pipeline
description: Finally, the automation that keeps hoopR healthy. R-CMD-check.yaml runs R CMD check across a macOS/Windows/Ubuntu matrix on push, PR, and a weekly cron, with opt-in live-API test toggles supplied via secrets. pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the documentation site (configured by _pkgdown.yml, which groups the reference index by data-source family), and rhub.yaml fans out cross-platform checks for CRAN submission. Together they enforce that every layer in this tour stays installable and documented.
languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' triggers (push/pull_request/schedule), a matrix to test across OS/R-version combinations in parallel, and repository secrets to inject API credentials so live-API tests run without committing keys.
